The map x->cx sends it homomorphically into the actual corner cBc: (cx)(cy)=cxy since xc=x. The local LEFT-regular identity gives cxyx=cxy. Left multiply by x and use xc=x to obtain xyx=xy. Thus EVERY principal left ideal Bc is a GLOBAL LEFT regular band, not just its local corner.

For arbitrary a,b,c put u=abc,v=abcac. Both belong to D_c. In ANY band uv=v and vu=u: uv=(abc)^2ac=v, while vu=abcacabc reduces the middle(ca)^2 to ca and then(abc)^2 to abc=u. Hence u R v in D_c. A LEFT regular band has singleton R-classes, so u=v. This proves xyz=xyzxz. Conversely substitute the actual corner identity e as z and x,y in eBe: xy=xyxe=xyx. Thus the short identity is EXACTLY W_L, with no global-left-regular assumption on B.

This also gives the previously stated global-L/right-normal characterization DIRECTLY. If x L y in B, xy=x,yx=y. In that quotient the short identity abc=abcac reduces by right regularity first to bcac and then bac, so abc=bac: the quotient is RIGHT normal. Conversely a right-normal quotient with L-kernel equates u=abc,v=abcac (right-normal implies right regular and reduces abcac to abac to bac to abc); u R v universally as above, and kernel L gives equality.
